given.part: An open loan's `dueOn` is before today (UTC)
given.why: Loans lent on 03-02 are due 03-16, and the clock is moved to 03-17 before the job runs.

given.part: it has no reminder recorded today
given.why: The loans are freshly created and the job runs once, so no reminder exists yet.

then.part: Asks the Notifications API to notify the loan's member
then.why: `fakeNotifications.sent` must hold each loan's own memberId, loanId and dueOn, with length 2.

then.part: then records a reminder for today
then.why: The reminders table must hold sent_on 2026-03-17, which differs from dueOn 03-16, so recording the wrong date would fail.
B3 covers it: a refused loan must have no recorded reminder, so recording before asking would fail there. mutants.json lists this ordering as not mutated for the same reason.

given.part: An open loan already has a reminder recorded today
given.why: The first run records loan1, and the second run is the same day with loan1 already reminded.
loan2 is overdue but is returned before the job runs.
Member-3's loan is due exactly on 03-17, the day of the run, so it tests the boundary.

then.why: `sent` must match exactly [{loanId: loan1}], so a second send for loan1, or any send for the returned or not-yet-due loan, would fail.

given.why: The fake refuses loan1 with the reason 'Notifications API answered 503'.
Only a refusal reason is faked. No service test sets up an unreachable API, and B5 has no test for a failed connection either.

then.why: The reminders table must contain only loan2's row.

then.part: logs `reminder.failed` at `warn` with `loanId` and the refusal's `error`
then.why: `toContainEqual` pins level, event, loanId and the exact error text.

then.part: carries on with the other loans
then.why: loan1 is refused and loan2 was lent later, so loan2 only gets its reminder if the job continues past the failure.

given.part: The job has handled every overdue loan
given.why: Three overdue loans are handled, with one refused.

then.why: The last log entry must equal level info, event reminders.finished and fields {sent: 2, failed: 1}.

given.why: A reminder object is passed straight to the real client.

then.part: Sends `POST {NOTIFY_URL}/notifications` with JSON `{ memberId, template: "loan-overdue", data: { loanId, dueOn } }`
then.why: The captured request is compared exactly on method, path, content-type and body.
202, 200 and 204 are each accepted, so an `=== 200` check would fail.

then.part: any other answer ... as refused, with a reason naming the status
then.why: A 400 must give kind refused with a reason containing '400'.

then.part: a failed connection as refused, with a reason saying the API was unreachable
then.why: No test simulates a network error, so neither the refusal on a failed connection nor the 'unreachable' reason is checked.
